frontier.hypothesis: Because loop 2's preheader is now measured C-inert and target's copies provably need no second use, the deciding condition lives in the RTL that the rest of the function hands to local-alloc - and the only place it can still be reached from C is the region OUTSIDE the two preheaders (the top-guard block, the loop bodies, and the byte-exact function tail), whose register pressure and pseudo lifetimes set the tie-break.
frontier.mechanism: s9 established the tie rule from the .lreg dump: when the base add's addend carries REG_DEAD, local-alloc's combine_regs ties the destination to the addend's hard register and no copy appears; when it does not, the copy appears with target's exact register numbers. s11 proves the addend's REG_DEAD status cannot be changed from inside loop 2's preheader (47 spellings, one score) and cannot be changed by a downstream use (no purchase site exists in target). What has never been probed is whether combine_regs declines for a NON-liveness reason - a register-class conflict, an allocno-priority ordering, or the destination pseudo already being tied to another allocno - which is set by the rest of the function.
frontier.next_probe: Generate the -da .lreg/.greg dumps for V1 (harness: tmp/grind/func_80017848/s10/dump.sh, re-pathed) and diff local-alloc's treatment of loop 1's base add against loop 2's IN THE SAME DUMP - they differ in outcome, so the deciding guard is visible side by side. Identify which combine_regs guard fires for loop 2, then look for a plain-C construct OUTSIDE loop 2's preheader (top-guard block spelling, loop-body spelling, tail spelling) that reproduces loop 1's condition for loop 2. Do NOT re-probe loop 2's preheader spelling, declaration order, a fresh read at loop 2's guard, or any second-use carrier - all four are measured dead this session.

frontier.hypothesis: A fresh-seed permuter campaign anchored on the V1 chassis is the highest-yield remaining modality (carried unchanged from s10's frontier #3, and now strengthened: s11 shows the hand-reachable structural neighbourhood of V1 is exhausted, so an automated search over spellings a human would not write is the natural next step).
frontier.mechanism: s4's win (14 -> 12) was invisible to the permuter's own ranking and only appeared when every output was re-scored with the engine. The V1 chassis is three levers deeper than s4's and has never been permuted. s11 additionally establishes that the search should be anchored OUTSIDE loop 2's preheader, since that region is inert - a permuter run confined to it would be guaranteed to find nothing.
frontier.next_probe: Launch tools/permuter_campaign.py on memory/grind/func_80017848/candidate.c with the PERM region spanning the top-guard block, loop 1 and the function tail (NOT loop 2's preheader). Wait IN-TURN with `permuter_campaign.py wait --dir <ws>` (one blocking call per fresh-seed window, ~20-30 windows per the fresh-seed discipline), re-score EVERY output with `sandbox --disable all` rather than trusting the permuter score, and `harvest --stop` before writing the outcome.

frontier.hypothesis: The three residual instructions are a pure SWAP of a load and a copy between two adjacent sites, and the instruction count already matches target exactly (127) - so the remaining gap may be a single allocator decision that a different but equivalent PROLOGUE/callee-save shape would flip, rather than anything in the loop code at all.
frontier.mechanism: Target's prologue saves s0,s1,s2,s3,s4,s5,ra into a 0x40 frame and moves all four parameters into callee-saved registers before the first compare. Ours matches byte for byte, but the ORDER in which those pseudos are created and die determines allocno priority (reg_n_refs and live length), which is the input to the combine_regs tie-break that s9 identified. Nothing in ten sessions has probed whether the parameter-homing region is a lever, because it has always been byte-exact and therefore looked settled.
frontier.next_probe: Sweep equivalent spellings of the parameter/top region that keep the prologue byte-exact but change pseudo creation order and reference counts - e.g. reading the four parameters into named locals in different orders, moving the `slot_a == slot_b` early return above/below the parameter uses, and splitting the two >=0 top guards into separate statements - re-scoring each with tmp/grind/func_80017848/s11/score.sh. Any cell scoring 2 or below gets disassembled with tmp/grind/func_80017848/s11/dis2.sh.
